title: Soundctuary Clahane, County Clare, Ireland - rather noisy sea
author: alfa00 (Soundctuary)
notes: Rough Atlantic sea on the Co. Clare coast, dense continuous breaker roar. FLAC 48k stereo (LR corr 0.57), very steady level over 8 min (+/-3 dB), loud (-15.5 LUFS). No voices/birds/tonal intrusions (tonal screen clean), no rain. Occasional brief HF spray streaks. Less distinct individual crash rhythm than surf-2 - a wall-of-surf layer.

title: North Sea Storm, Slaughden, UK
author: David Pitt
notes: Fierce northerly North Sea storm, big surf ~5 m away on a shingle beach (MixPre-6 II + 2x MKH 8020, mics crouched behind a breakwater). Clear 8-10 s crash/shingle-drag cycles. Low end is highly L/R-coherent (0.94) so it is acoustic surf roar, not mic buffeting. Caveats: only a 320 kbps MP3 is published (44.1k); very dark/LF-heavy because the mics were heavily wrapped (little above 2 kHz) - may wan

title: Ploumanach, Lighthouse - Heavy waves crushing into rocks
author: Yponomeutaneko
notes: Optional extra: wild waves crashing into the granite rocks at Ploumanac'h lighthouse (Oktava MK012 ORTF, FLAC 48k). Rocky-shore perspective, deep booming LF. Segment chosen to avoid a 14-sample clip at 14.2 s and windier stretches after ~110 s (LF L/R coherence drops). Only 95 s; one single full-scale sample at 39.9 s (inaudible). Very LF-heavy.

title: Vyzuoneles, Lithuania, under the rain
author: alas23/sala
notes: Short heavy rain recorded under park trees: rain on foliage/ground, very even broadband texture (250 Hz-8 kHz), wide stereo (LR corr 0.07), FLAC 44.1k. Tonal screen clean (no voices/birds/traffic), no thunder, no roof/umbrella sound. Rain builds during the first ~50 s and the file fades at the end, so segment 40-212 s.

title: Piechowice, Poland - (888) Strong wind
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Strong gale roaring through a forest, big gust swells (~205-230 s, ~300 s, ~360 s). DPA 4560 + MixPre-6 II, FLAC 48k. 60-400 Hz L/R coherence ~0.9-0.99, so the roar is acoustic, not mic buffeting. Clean tonal screen (no birds/voices). Caveat: it is tree roar rather than wind on open rocks; reads as a generic storm roar.

title: Glendale Ln, Beaufort, SC 29902, USA - Violent Windstorm
author: SoundHunter
notes: Hurricane Helene windstorm at 1 am: violent gusting wind in trees, recorded through a slightly opened top-floor window (EM272 omnis, wind muffs, HPF), FLAC 44.1k. Segment avoids low thumps (~290 s, ~450 s) and the insect tones that appear after ~590 s. Caveats: semi-indoor perspective, faint raindrops. CC BY 3.0, so credit is required.

title: Wedmore, Somerset, UK - Big Thunder Storm
author: bygravemax (radio aporee maps)
notes: Wedmore roll A: precursor rumble, crack at ~6.7 s, long roll, natural decay to the recordist's fade at 54.9 s (digital silence after). 744 + KFM6, FLAC 48k, almost no rain. Clean.

title: Wedmore, Somerset, UK - Big Thunder Storm
author: bygravemax (radio aporee maps)
notes: Wedmore roll B: very loud crack at ~59.0 s then a ~55 s roll, ending at the recordist's fade (115.45). Caveat: a few sub-ms flat-topped samples at the cracks (~59.0-59.9 s), masked by the crack.

title: Wedmore, Somerset, UK - Big Thunder Storm
author: bygravemax (radio aporee maps)
notes: Wedmore roll C: ~2.5 s building precursor rumble, cracks at ~119.3 and ~120.5 s, long roll and natural tail to 171.86 (fade into digital silence). Brief flat-topping at ~123.3-124.0 s (sub-ms).

title: Wedmore, Somerset, UK - Big Thunder Storm
author: bygravemax (radio aporee maps)
notes: Wedmore roll D: sharp onset at ~192.0 s, peak ~194.2 s, decays to near silence by 223.6 (recordist fade). Start trimmed to 191.6 to skip 2 s of floor containing a faint tonal blip. Sub-ms flat-topping at 194.2-194.7 s.

title: Thunder (twice) on neighbourhood, Kraków, Polska - (646 AB 18cm)
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Close thunder clap and roll ('thunderstorm passing close'): onset ~0.8 s from the noise floor, peak -4 dBFS at ~5 s, smooth ~32 dB decay. MKH 8020 AB 18 cm + MixPre-6 II, FLAC 48k, fairly narrow stereo (corr 0.94). Light urban/rain floor ~30 dB below peak, no voices/birds.

title: Thunder (twice) on neighbourhood, Kraków, Polska - (646 AB 18cm)
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Sharp crack at ~38.3 s (broadband up to ~3 kHz) followed by a rolling rumble, decaying by ~60 s. Smaller/more distant than thunder-5.

title: Thunder (twice) on neighbourhood, Kraków, Polska - (646 AB 18cm)
author: Piotrek Zyla
notes: Distant low rumble (energy almost all below 150 Hz, no crack), peak ~112 s, decays to the floor at ~119.5 s. Caveat: light rain hiss and a city floor ~20 dB below the rumble.

title: Tangara, Rio Acima, Brazil - Rain and thunder during the night, in Brazil
author: Felix Blume
notes: Felix Blume (Schoeps CCM4 ORTF + SD633; published as a 320 kbps MP3). Mid-distance rolling thunder from silence: gradual rumble onset ~43.5 s, peak ~50 s, rolls and decays to the floor by ~77 s. No rain at this point, and the tonal screen is clean.

title: Tangara, Rio Acima, Brazil - Rain and thunder during the night, in Brazil
author: Felix Blume
notes: Huge close strike: silent pre-roll, crack at ~480.5 s (to ~2 kHz), massive ~45 s roll. Cut at a local minimum about 26 dB below peak (529.0); apply a 1-2 s fade-out. If a longer natural tail is wanted, extend to 539.6 (a secondary rumble then full decay). Caveat: a faint night-insect chorus (~3 and ~5.3 kHz) about 50 dB below the peak, masked by beds.

title: Tangara, Rio Acima, Brazil - Rain and thunder during the night, in Brazil
author: Felix Blume
notes: Short sharp clap at ~1302.0 s with a second burst ~1310.5 s, back to the floor by ~1313 s. Caveat: steady light rain hiss throughout (floor about 24 dB below the peak); fade the edges.
